```python
import re

EMAIL_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{|}~-]+"
    r"@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"
    r"(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)+$"
)

def is_valid_email(email: str) -> bool:
    if not email or len(email) > 254:
        return False
    return bool(EMAIL_PATTERN.match(email))
```

Checks the shape of the address and blocks anything absurdly long. It won't catch every RFC edge case, but it's a solid everyday check.

For real signup forms, pair it with a confirmation email instead of trusting regex alone.
